answer: An agent marketplace uses a staking contract as its inlet: every identity must lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid for work, and the same tokens cannot back another identity during that period. Agents may wander through the shared garden of services, but creating 1,000 eligible identities ties up 100,000 tokens for a month. Splitting one balance across fake accounts buys no extra bidding capacity without proportional capital.
